source_text: Εἰ γὰρ εἰς γάμους αἰσθητοὺς ἄνθρωποι καλούμενοι, κἂν ἁπάντων ὦσι πενέστεροι, χρησάμενοι πολλάκις ἢ πριάμενοι ἱμάτιον καθαρὸν, οὕτω πρὸς τοὺς καλέσαντας αὐτοὺς ἀπαντῶσι· σὺ δὲ ὁ πρὸς γάμον κληθεὶς πνευματικὸν καὶ δεῖπνα βασιλικὰ, ἐννόησον, ἡλίκον ἂν εἴη δίκαιόν σε ἱμάτιον πρίασθαι· μᾶλλον δὲ οὐδὲ ἀγοράσαι χρεία, ἀλλ' αὐτός σοι δίδωσιν ὁ καλῶν δωρεὰν, ἵνα μηδὲ πενίαν προβαλέσθαι ἔχῃς. Τήρει τοίνυν ὅπερ ἔλαβες ἱμάτιον· ἂν γὰρ ἀπολέσῃς, χρήσασθαι οὐ δυνήσῃ λοιπὸν, οὐδὲ πρίασθαι· οὐδαμοῦ γὰρ πωλεῖται τοιοῦτον ἱμάτιον. Ἤκουσας, πῶς ἐστέναξαν οἱ πάλαι μυσταγωγηθέντες, καὶ τὸ στῆθος ἐπάταξαν τοῦ συνειδότος ἐνταῦθα διαναστήσαντος; Σκόπει τοίνυν, ἀγαπητὲ, μὴ καὶ σύ ποτε τοῦτο πάθῃ· πῶς δὲ οὐ πείσῃ, τὴν πονηρὰν συνήθειαν μὴ ἐκβαλὼν τῶν κακῶν; Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ πρώην εἶπον καὶ νῦν λέγω, καὶ λέγων οὐ παύσομαι, εἴ τις τὰ ἐλαττώματα τῶν τρόπων μὴ διώρθωσε μηδὲ παρεσκεύασεν ἑαυτῷ τὴν ἀρετὴν εὔκολον, μὴ βαπτιζέσθω. Τὰ μὲν γὰρ πρότερα ἁμαρτήματα ἀφεῖναι δύναται τὸ λουτρόν· δέος δὲ οὐ μικρὸν καὶ κίνδυνος οὐχ ὁ τυχὼν, μήποτε πάλιν ἐπ' αὐτὰ ἐπανέλθωμεν, καὶ γένηται ἡμῖν ἕλκος τὸ φάρμακον. Ὅσῳ γὰρ μείζων γέγονεν ἡ χάρις, τοσούτῳ πλείων ἡ κόλασις τοῖς μετὰ ταῦτα ἁμαρτάνουσιν. γʹ. Ἵνα οὖν μὴ πρὸς τὸν πρότερον ἐπανίωμεν ἐμετὸν, παιδεύσωμεν ἑαυτοὺς ἐντεῦθεν ἤδη. Ὅτι γὰρ δεῖ πρότερον μετανοήσαντας καὶ τῶν προτέρων ἀποστάντας κακῶν, οὕτω τῇ χάριτι προσιέναι, ἄκουσον τί μὲν Ἰωάννης φησὶ, τί δὲ ὁ τῶν ἀποστόλων κορυφαῖος τοῖς βαπτίζεσθαι μέλλουσιν· ἐκεῖνος μὲν γάρ φησι· Ποιήσατε καρπὸν ἄξιον τῆς μετανοίας, καὶ μὴ ἄρξησθε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, ὅτι Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ· οὗτος δὲ τοῖς ἐρωτῶσι πάλιν ἔλεγε· Μετανοήσατε, καὶ βαπτισθήτω ἕκαστος ὑμῶν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Ὁ δὲ μετανοῶν οὐκέτι τῶν αὐτῶν ἅπτεται πραγμάτων, ἐφ' οἷς μετενόησε· διὰ τοῦτο καὶ κελευόμεθα λέγειν· Ἀποτάσσομαί σοι, Σατανᾶ, ἵνα μηκέτι πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπανέλθωμεν. Καθάπερ οὖν ἐπὶ τῶν ζωγράφων γίνεται, οὕτω καὶ νῦν γινέσθω· καὶ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι τὰς σανίδας προθέντες, καὶ λευκὰς περιάγοντες γραμμὰς, καὶ τὰς βασιλικὰς ὑπογράφοντες εἰκόνας, πρὶν ἢ τῶν χρωμάτων ἐπαγαγεῖν τὴν ἀλήθειαν, μετ' ἐξουσίας ἁπάσης τὰ μὲν ἐξαλείφουσι, τὰ δὲ ἀντεγγράφουσι, καὶ διορθοῦντες τὰ ἡμαρτημένα καὶ μετατιθέντες τὰ κακῶς ἔχοντα· ἐπειδὰν δὲ τὴν βαφὴν λοιπὸν ἐπαγάγωσιν, οὐκέτι εἰσὶ κύριοι πάλιν ἐξαλεῖψαι καὶ ἀντεγγράψαι, ἐπεὶ τῷ κάλλει τῆς εἰκόνος λυμαίνονται, καὶ ἔγκλημα τὸ πρᾶγμα γίνεται· τοῦτο δὴ καὶ σὺ ποίησον· νόμισον εἰκόνα σοι τὴν ψυχὴν εἶναι. Πρὶν ἢ τοίνυν ἐπελθεῖν τὴν ἀληθῆ τοῦ Πνεύματος βαφὴν, ἐξάλειψον τὰς κακῶς ἐντεθείσας σοι συνηθείας· εἴτε ὀμνύναι, εἴτε ψεύδεσθαι, εἴτε ὑβρίζειν, εἴτε αἰσχρολογεῖν, εἴτε γελωτοποιεῖν, εἴτε ἄλλο τι τῶν τοιούτων τῶν μὴ νενομισμένων συνήθειαν ἔχεις ποιεῖν, ἔξελε τὴν συνήθειαν, ἵνα μὴ πάλιν πρὸς αὐτὴν ἐπανέλθῃς μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα. Τὰ ἁμαρτήματα ἀφανίζει τὸ λουτρὸν, τὴν συνήθειαν διόρθωσον σὺ, ἵνα τῶν χρωμάτων ἐπενεχθέντων καὶ λαμψάσης τῆς βασιλικῆς εἰκόνος, μηκέτι λοιπὸν ἐξαλείφῃς, καὶ τραύματα καὶ οὐλὰς ἐμποιῇς τῷ παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ δοθέντι σοι κάλλει.
thought_title: The garment of baptism and the painter's board
orientation: Chrysostom is addressing the catechumens preparing for baptism, urging them to reform their habits before receiving the washing of regeneration.
pass_a_gloss: For if people invited to perceptible weddings, even if they are poorer than all, having often borrowed or bought a clean garment, in this way go to meet those who invited them; but you, the one invited to a spiritual wedding and royal banquets, consider how great a garment it would be just for you to buy; rather, there is not even need to buy, but the one who invites gives it to you himself as a gift, so that you may not even have poverty to put forward as an excuse. Guard therefore the garment which you received; for if you lose it, you will no longer be able to borrow it, nor to buy it; for nowhere is such a garment sold. You heard how those initiated long ago groaned, and struck their breast when the conscience rose up there? Consider therefore, beloved, lest you too ever suffer this; and how will you not suffer it, if you do not cast out the wicked habit of evils? For this reason I both said before and now say, and will not stop saying: if someone has not corrected the defects of his ways nor prepared virtue to be easy for himself, let him not be baptized. For the washing is able to forgive former sins; but there is no small fear and no ordinary danger, lest we return again to them, and the medicine becomes a wound for us. For by as much as the grace has become greater, by so much is the punishment greater for those who sin after these things. 3. So that we may not return to our former vomit, let us train ourselves from now on. For that it is necessary first to repent and to stand away from former evils, and in this way to approach the grace, hear what John says, and what the chief of the apostles says to those about to be baptized; for that one says: Produce fruit worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say among yourselves, that we have Abraham as father; and this one said again to those asking: Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. And the one who repents no longer touches the same matters over which he repented; for this reason we are also commanded to say: I renounce you, Satan, so that we may no longer return to him. Just as therefore happens in the case of painters, so let it also happen now; for they, having set out the boards, and having drawn white lines around, and having sketched the royal images, before bringing on the truth of the colors, with all authority they erase some things, and write in others instead, both correcting the mistakes and changing the things that are badly placed; but when they have brought on the dye at last, they are no longer able again to erase and write in instead, since they damage the beauty of the image, and the matter becomes a charge; do this very thing then; consider your soul to be an image. Before therefore the true dye of the Spirit comes upon it, erase the habits badly implanted in you; whether you have a habit of swearing oaths, or lying, or insulting, or speaking shamefully, or jesting, or doing any other of such things that are not lawful, remove the habit, so that you may not return to it again after baptism. The washing destroys the sins; you correct the habit, so that when the colors have been brought on and the royal image has shone, you may no longer erase it, and make wounds and scars in the beauty given to you by God.

choices.why: The glossary fixes 'washing of regeneration' for the full phrase; here alone it is the washing, i.e. baptism.
The glossary requires this exact rendering for the baptismal renunciation.
rejected: I turn away from you, Satan

choices.why: In the painter metaphor, βαφή is the dye or color application; keeping 'dye' preserves the image of the painter's final act.
The glossary bans 'swearing' and 'vows' for ὅρκοι; 'oaths' and 'swearing oaths' keep the literal sense.
The compound verb means to go back up or return; 'return again' captures the iterative force.
In context, damaging the image becomes an accusation or legal charge against the painter; 'charge' keeps the forensic sense.

pass_b_english: When people are invited to an ordinary wedding, even if they are poorer than everyone else, they often borrow or buy a clean garment and go to their hosts dressed in that. But you have been invited to a spiritual wedding and a royal banquet. Consider what kind of garment you ought to buy. Yet there is no need to buy one at all: the one who invites you gives it to you as a gift, so that you cannot even plead poverty as an excuse. Guard the garment you have received, then. If you lose it, you will no longer be able to borrow or buy another, because such a garment is not sold anywhere.

You heard how those who were initiated long ago groaned and struck their chests when their conscience rose up against them here. Take care, beloved, that you never suffer the same thing. And how will you not suffer it, if you do not cast out the wicked habit of evil deeds? This is why I said before and say now, and will not stop saying: if anyone has not corrected the defects of his character and made virtue easy for himself, let him not be baptized. The washing can forgive former sins, but there is no small fear and no ordinary danger that we may return to them again, and the medicine may become a wound for us. For the greater the grace has been, the greater the punishment for those who sin afterward.

So that we may not return to our former vomit, let us train ourselves from this point on. For you must first repent and turn away from your former evils, and only then approach the grace. Listen to what John says, and what the chief of the apostles says to those about to be baptized. John says: “Bear fruit worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say among yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father’” (Matthew 3:8). And Peter said to those who asked: “Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ” (Acts 2:38). The one who repents no longer touches the same deeds over which he repented. This is why we are commanded to say: “I renounce you, Satan,” so that we may never return to him again.

Let it be now as it is with painters. They set out their panels, draw white outlines, and sketch the royal images. Before they apply the truth of the colors, they have full authority to erase some lines and draw others in their place, correcting what is wrong and changing what is badly placed. But once they apply the dye, they are no longer free to erase and redraw, because that ruins the beauty of the image and the thing becomes a charge against them. Do the same yourself. Consider your soul to be an image. Before the true dye of the Spirit comes upon you, erase the bad habits that have been implanted in you. Whether you have a habit of swearing oaths, lying, insulting, speaking shamefully, playing the fool, or doing any other such thing that is not permitted, remove the habit, so that you will not return to it again after baptism. The washing destroys sins; you must correct the habit, so that when the colors have been applied and the royal image shines, you will no longer erase it and inflict wounds and scars on the beauty God has given you.

problems.source_quote: Ποιήσατε καρπὸν ἄξιον τῆς μετανοίας, καὶ μὴ ἄρξησθε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, ὅτι Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ
problems.why: The source attributes this to John the Baptist, but the English cites Matthew. The source pairs John with Peter, and the quote matches Luke 3:8 (where John says this), not Matthew 3:8-9. The work brief identifies this as John the Baptist speaking in section 12.
problems.ruling: Quote matches Luke 3:8, not Matthew 3:8-9; wrong scripture reference misleads the reader.

fixed: Changed citation from Matthew 3:8-9 to Luke 3:8, since the source attributes the quotation to John the Baptist and the wording matches Luke 3:8.

problems.why: This is Matthew 3:9, not Luke 3:8. The LXX/Septuagint citation follows Matthew's wording.

last_rejected.ruling: 'Let him not be baptized' correctly renders μη βαπτιζέσθω as a prohibition; no modality error.

last_rejected.why: 'Playing the fool' suggests buffoonery; γελωτοποιεῖν means making others laugh, jesting, clowning—broader than mere foolishness.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Playing the fool' is within γελωτοποιεῖν's range of jesting/clowning; not a meaning change.
